docs.text: HardFOC driver ADS9324 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the Texas Instruments ADS9324 16-channel, 16-bit simultaneous-sampling SAR ADC. It brings the chip up in 1-lane SDOUT mode, programs each channel's PGA range, input type, filter and calibration, and reads all 16 channels from one CONVST edge, on any MCU with an SPI controller and two GPIOs. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a class that runs one SPI transfer with chip select held low, and a class that drives CONVST, reads DRDY and waits; it does the rest: the initialisation sequence, register banks, 24-bit frames, PGA nibble packing, the conversion burst and the conversion to volts. 16-channel simultaneous-sampling SAR ADC with analog front end ADS9324 Texas Instruments Conversion 16 SAR ADCs, 16 bits, up to 1 MSPS per channel, all sampled on the CONVST falling edge Inputs 1 MΩ PGA per channel: differential, single-ended or open-wire safe; ±2.5, ±5, ±6.25, ±10, ±12.5 V Interface SPI mode 0 up to 60 MHz, 24-bit register frames; conversion data on 1, 2, 4 or 8 lanes Control pins CONVST, DRDY/ALARM, RESET (active low), REFSEL Supply AVDD_5V 4.75 V to 5.25 V, AVDD_1V8 1.7 V to 1.9 V, IOVDD 1.7 V to 3.6 V; internal 4.096 V reference Package 64-pin VQFN (RSK), 8 mm × 8 mm, –40 °C to +125 °C Driver mode 1-lane, 16-bit conversion data on SDOUT (GEN_CFG3 = 0x0032 ), sharing the register SPI bus Datasheet (SBASB22) · Product page What you get ¶ One object per chip. ADS9324<Spi, Host> owns the register banks, the 24-bit frames and the cached channel settings. See API guide . Bring-up in one call. EnsureInitialized() waits for the supplies, resets the chip, selects 1-lane SDOUT output and checks DEVICE_ID. See Quickstart . A front end per channel. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: initialise, configure channels, calibrate, read and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with adc an ads9324::ADS9324<MySpi, MyHost> over the port . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One ADS9324<Spi, Host> object per chip. Its methods fall into five groups: Group Methods Bring-up EnsureInitialized() , IsInitialized() , SoftwareReset() , ReadDeviceId() Channels ConfigureChannel() , ConfigureAllChannels() , GetChannelConfig() , SetChannelOffset() , SetChannelGain() Data interface SetDataFormat() , GetDataFormat() , SetDigitalInterface() , SetChannelCountMode() Pins and power SetAlarmPin() , ProgramWindowComparator() , SetPowerDown() Reading ReadSnapshot() , ReadChannel() , CountToVoltage() , GetDiagnostics() Configuration calls return bool : false means the channel index was out of range or the call did not complete. Reads return a Snapshot or ReadResult with an error field. Nothing throws or allocates. Channels are numbered 0 to 15 in the API (AIN1 to AIN16 on the chip). Initialise ¶ if ( ! adc . EnsureInitialized ()) { // 30 ms settle, SW reset, GEN_CFG3 = 0x0032, DEVICE_ID const uint16_t id = adc . ReadDeviceId (); // 0x0004 on a healthy ADS9324, 0 when SDOUT is dead std :: printf ( "ADS9324 init failed, DEVICE_ID = 0x%04X 
 " , id ); return false ; } // Later calls return at once; EnsureInitialized(true) runs the whole sequence again. EnsureInitialized() runs the datasheet's 1-lane sequence ( Registers and SPI frames ) and fails when DEVICE_ID is not 0x0004 . Every read and every snapshot needs it to have succeeded. Define CONFIG_ADS9324_SKIP_DEVICE_ID_CHECK to skip the ID check during bench bring-up ( Configuration ). Configure the channels ¶ // AIN1..AIN4: ±10 V differential, wide bandwidth for a fast current-sense signal. ads9324 :: ChannelConfig current ; current . type = ads9324 :: InputType :: Differential ; current . range = ads9324 :: InputRange :: PlusMinus10V ; current . bandwidth = ads9324 :: PgaBandwidth :: Wide ; // AIN5..AIN16: ±2.5 V single-ended sensors that may come unplugged. ads9324 :: ChannelConfig sensor ; sensor . type = ads9324 :: InputType :: SingleEndedOpenWireSafe ; sensor . range = ads9324 :: InputRange :: PlusMinus2V5 ; for ( uint8_t ch = 0 ; ch < ads9324 :: kNumChannels ; ++ ch ) { if ( ! adc . ConfigureChannel ( ch , ch < 4 ? current : sensor )) { return false ; // ch out of range, or the bus failed } } ChannelConfig field Default Values type Differential Differential , SingleEnded , SingleEndedOpenWireSafe range PlusMinus5V PlusMinus2V5 , PlusMinus5V , PlusMinus6V25 , PlusMinus10V , PlusMinus12V5 bandwidth Low Low (25.5 kHz), Wide (280 kHz to 350 kHz) common_mode_correct false Common-mode error correction Each ConfigureChannel() call is a read-modify-write of two registers (about eight SPI frames). The driver keeps the last configuration per channel; GetChannelConfig(ch) returns it, and the voltage conversion uses its range. Until you configure a channel, the driver assumes the compile-time default range, which is ±5 V, the chip's reset value. EnsureInitialized() does not write the defaults to the chip: if you change them with CONFIG_ADS9324_RANGE_* ( Configuration ), call ConfigureAllChannels() so the chip and the driver agree. PGA and calibration explains the encodings. Calibrate offset and gain ¶ // Offset: 10-bit two's complement in quarter LSBs, added before the gain (Equation 1). // Channel 0 reads 10 LSB high with its input shorted: subtract 40 quarter LSBs. if ( ! adc . SetChannelOffset ( 0 , -40 )) { return false ; } // Gain: 14-bit two's complement; the chip multiplies by (1 + GAN / 65536). // Channel 0 reads 0.5 % high: GAN = -0.005 * 65536 = -328. The driver keeps the low 14 bits. const int16_t gan = -328 ; if ( ! adc . SetChannelGain ( 0 , static_cast < uint16_t > ( gan ))) { return false ; } The offset is in quarter LSBs (−128 to +127.75 LSB); the gain multiplies by 1 + GAN / 65536 (about ±12.5 %). Measure with the real source impedance connected: the correction is for the whole signal chain. Read ¶ const ads9324 :: Snapshot snap = adc . ReadSnapshot (); // all 16 channels, same sampling instant if ( snap . ok ()) { for ( uint8_t ch = 0 ; ch < ads9324 :: kNumChannels ; ++ ch ) { if ( snap . hasChannel ( ch )) { std :: printf ( "AIN%u: %6d %.4f V 
 " , ch + 1U , snap . count [ ch ], static_cast < double > ( snap . voltage [ ch ])); } } } // One channel: still one full conversion; the others are discarded. const ads9324 :: ReadResult r = adc . ReadChannel ( 3 ); if ( r . ok ()) { const float again = adc . CountToVoltage ( 3 , r . count ); // same value as r.voltage ( void ) again ; } ReadSnapshot() is one CONVST edge: all channels are sampled at the same instant. valid_mask has a bit for each channel clocked out, and hasChannel(ch) tests it. ReadChannel() runs a full snapshot and keeps one channel; call ReadSnapshot() once when you need more than one. The SPI burst is 32 bytes at the default 16-bit word length. At the examples' 8 MHz clock that is 32 µs on the bus; see Hardware for the rate this allows. Change the data format and word length ¶ // Offset-binary coding on the wire; the driver still returns two's-complement counts. if ( ! adc . SetDataFormat ( ads9324 :: DataFormat :: OffsetBinary )) { return false ; } // 24-bit words on SDOUT (48-byte bursts); the driver uses the top 16 bits as the code. return adc . SetDigitalInterface ( ads9324 :: DoutLaneMode :: Lane1 , ads9324 :: DoutLength :: Bits24 , true ); Both calls rewrite GEN_CFG3. Snapshot::count stays two's complement whatever the wire format. Keep DoutLaneMode::Lane1 with data on SDOUT: ReadSnapshot() reads SDOUT only, so another lane setting stops the data from reaching it. Read fewer channels ¶ SetChannelCountMode(mode, ch_sel) writes ANA_CFG2 so the chip converts and outputs 8, 4 or 2 channels, which shortens the burst. Channel numbers in reduced modes The chip outputs a fixed set of channels in these modes, taken from both ends (Table 7-12): with ChannelCountMode::Eight and ch_sel 0 it sends AIN1 to AIN4 and AIN13 to AIN16. ReadSnapshot() stores the n th word of the burst as channel n , so count[4] then holds AIN13, not AIN5, and the voltage uses channel 4's range. Use ChannelCountMode::All16 (the default) unless you map the channels yourself. Window comparator and alarm pin ¶ // Window comparator on AIN1. Thresholds are compared with the top 8 bits of the code, so one // step is 256 LSB: +64 is +FS/2, -16 is -FS/8. Alert while AIN1 is outside that window. if ( ! adc . ProgramWindowComparator ( 0 , 64 , -16 )) { return false ; } // Route the comparator to the DRDY/ALARM pin. DRDY polling then no longer works: // give the port HasDrdy() == false, or switch back with SetAlarmPin(AlarmPinMode::Drdy). return adc . SetAlarmPin ( ads9324 :: AlarmPinMode :: DwcAlert ); AlarmPinMode DRDY/ALARM carries Drdy (default) Conversion ready, active high DwcAlert Any enabled window comparator out of its window AdcCalDone On-chip calibration finished OrMasked OR of the alarm flags selected by the mask SetAlarmPin(mode, true) inverts the pin's polarity. With the pin inverted or muxed away from Drdy , the driver's DRDY poll reads the wrong signal: give the port HasDrdy() == false for that time. Power down ¶ if ( ! adc . SetPowerDown ( true )) { // standby: AFE and reference off, about 6.5 mW return false ; } // ... later return adc . SetPowerDown ( false ); // the reference needs time to settle before accurate samples Standby powers down the analog front ends and the internal reference. The registers keep their values. The reference takes up to 30 ms to settle again (with 1 µF on REFCAP). Handle errors ¶ const ads9324 :: Snapshot snap = adc . ReadSnapshot (); switch ( snap . error ) { case ads9324 :: Error :: Ok : break ; case ads9324 :: Error :: NotInitialized : // EnsureInitialized() never succeeded adc . EnsureInitialized ( true ); break ; case ads9324 :: Error :: Timeout : // DRDY stayed low for DRDY_TIMEOUT_US std :: printf ( "no DRDY: check CONVST and the DRDY/ALARM mux 
 " ); break ; default : break ; } const ads9324 :: Diagnostics d = adc . GetDiagnostics (); // software counters, no SPI traffic std :: printf ( "snapshots %lu, errors %lu 
 " , static_cast < unsigned long > ( d . snapshots ), static_cast < unsigned long > ( d . errors )); Signal Meaning What to do EnsureInitialized() returns false Reset frame failed or DEVICE_ID was not 0x0004 Check ReadDeviceId() , then wiring and supplies Error::NotInitialized A read before a successful EnsureInitialized() Initialise first Error::Timeout DRDY did not rise within DRDY_TIMEOUT_US (1000 µs) CONVST wiring, DRDY polarity, SetAlarmPin() Error::InvalidChannel ReadChannel() with a channel above 15 Use 0 to 15 Error::SpiError The requested channel was not in the burst A reduced channel-count mode is active A configuration call returns false Channel above 15 Use 0 to 15 GetDiagnostics() returns the software counters ( snapshots , errors ) and the cached interface settings without touching the bus. Bus errors are not detected SpiInterface::transfer() returns nothing, so the driver cannot see a failed SPI transaction: it reads whatever arrived. DEVICE_ID at start-up is the only end-to-end check. If your SDK reports transfer errors, count them in your port. Troubleshooting maps symptoms to causes.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the chip. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one ADS9324 object, whose public methods are listed from inc/ads9324.hpp. The core packs 24-bit register frames, selects register banks, merges the PGA nibbles and unpacks conversion bursts. It reaches the hardware only through two CRTP contracts in inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp: SpiInterface (one transfer method) and HostInterface (CONVST, DRDY and two delays). The platform port is the only code you write: two small classes, or one class implementing both. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/ads9324.hpp ADS9324 public methods ; inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface, HostInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The three layers ¶ Layer Where You change it Core : ADS9324<Spi, Host> , uses the two contracts only ads9324.hpp , ads9324.ipp Never, for a new board Contracts : SpiInterface , HostInterface , six methods of your port ads9324_spi_interface.hpp Never Platform port : your classes, over your SDK Your project Once per MCU or board ( Porting ) Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test mock. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. How one call reaches the chip ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant D as ADS9324 core participant S as Your SpiInterface participant H as Your HostInterface A->>D: ConfigureChannel(9, cfg) D->>D: channel 9 = AIN10: bank AIN9-16, local 1, odd nibble D->>S: BANK_SEL = 0x0004 (only if the bank changed) D->>S: GEN_CFG1 read command, then a dummy frame (read PGA_CONFIG) D->>S: PGA_CONFIG with the new high nibble D->>S: PGA_BW_SEL read and write D-->>A: true A->>D: ReadSnapshot() D->>H: ConvstWrite(true), DelayUs(1), ConvstWrite(false) D->>H: DrdyRead() every 1 µs until high D->>S: transfer(32 bytes) D-->>A: Snapshot: counts, volts, valid_mask Why CRTP ¶ The contracts are class template parameters, not virtual base classes. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: ADS9324<MySpi, MyHost> . One class can implement both contracts and be passed twice, as the ESP32 examples do. What the driver keeps in RAM ¶ The object caches the selected register bank (so a burst of writes to one bank costs one BANK_SEL frame), each channel's last ChannelConfig (for CountToVoltage() ), the data format, lane and word-length settings, the channel-count mode and two counters. It reads nothing back from the chip except DEVICE_ID and the shared PGA, bandwidth and comparator registers it read-modify-writes. Your application talks to one ADS9324 object, whose public methods are listed from inc/ads9324.hpp. The core packs 24-bit register frames, selects register banks, merges the PGA nibbles and unpacks conversion bursts. It reaches the hardware only through two CRTP contracts in inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp: SpiInterface (one transfer method) and HostInterface (CONVST, DRDY and two delays). The platform port is the only code you write: two small classes, or one class implementing both. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/ads9324.hpp ADS9324 public methods ; inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface, HostInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py .

docs.text: The contracts are class template parameters, not virtual base classes. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: ADS9324<MySpi, MyHost> . One class can implement both contracts and be passed twice, as the ESP32 examples do.
docs.title: Why CRTP

docs.text: The object caches the selected register bank (so a burst of writes to one bank costs one BANK_SEL frame), each channel's last ChannelConfig (for CountToVoltage() ), the data format, lane and word-length settings, the channel-count mode and two counters. It reads nothing back from the chip except DEVICE_ID and the shared PGA, bandwidth and comparator registers it read-modify-writes.

Configuration ¶ The compile-time defaults of the driver: what each CONFIG_ADS9324_* macro changes and how to set it. Run-time settings (range, input type, bandwidth, offset, gain, data format) are method calls; the API guide covers them. The macros below only change the values the driver starts with. They are read in inc/ads9324_config.hpp into the ADS9324_CFG namespace. Defaults ¶ Each macro below is CONFIG_ADS9324_ followed by the name in the first column. Name Effect; default without it RANGE_12V5 , RANGE_10V , RANGE_2V5 Range in the driver's channel cache, DEFAULT_RANGE ; ±5 V SINGLE_ENDED Input type in the cache, DEFAULT_INPUT_TYPE ; differential PGA_WIDE Filter in the cache, DEFAULT_BANDWIDTH ; low bandwidth OFFSET_BINARY Data format written to GEN_CFG3 at initialisation, DEFAULT_FORMAT ; two's complement SKIP_DEVICE_ID_CHECK EnsureInitialized() stops requiring DEVICE_ID = 0x0004 ; check on POWER_ON_DELAY_MS Wait before the first frame, in ms; 30 (t PU ) RESET_DELAY_MS Wait after the software reset, in ms; 1 DRDY_TIMEOUT_US DRDY poll budget after CONVST, in 1 µs steps; 1000 CONV_FALLBACK_US Wait after CONVST when HasDrdy() is false , in µs; 10 The range, input type and bandwidth defaults only seed the driver's cache: EnsureInitialized() does not write them to the chip, whose reset state is ±5 V differential, low bandwidth. Call ConfigureAllChannels() after initialisation when you change them, so the chip matches. Do not lower POWER_ON_DELAY_MS below 30 unless your REFCAP capacitor is smaller than the datasheet's 1 µF, and keep CONV_FALLBACK_US above the conversion time (1.25 µs without oversampling). Set them ¶ CMake ESP-IDF target_compile_definitions ( my_app PRIVATE CONFIG_ADS9324_RANGE_10V CONFIG_ADS9324_DRDY_TIMEOUT_US=200 ) # main/CMakeLists.txt, after idf_component_register() target_compile_definitions ( ${ COMPONENT_LIB } PRIVATE CONFIG_ADS9324_RANGE_10V CONFIG_ADS9324_DRDY_TIMEOUT_US=200 ) Define the macros for every translation unit that includes ads9324.hpp : the driver is a template, so each one compiles its own copy, and different values in different files break the one-definition rule. Fixed settings ¶ These are constants, not macros: DEFAULT_LANES ( DoutLaneMode::Lane1 ), DEFAULT_LENGTH ( DoutLength::Bits16 ) and DEFAULT_DATA_ON_SDOUT ( true ) give GEN_CFG3 = 0x0032 . Change them at run time with SetDigitalInterface() .

docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between your MCU and an ADS9324, with which bus settings, and the board-level details that decide whether the first read works. All values here come from the ADS9324 datasheet (SBASB22, December 2025). When they disagree with a board's schematic, the schematic wins for pin numbers; the datasheet wins for limits. Host interface pins ¶ The driver uses the register SPI port for everything: register frames on SDI, register read-back and conversion data on SDOUT. The eight parallel data lanes stay unused. Signal (pin), direction Notes SCLK (37), in SPI clock; idles low SDI (36), in Latched on the SCLK rising edge SDOUT (38), out Register data and 1-lane conversion data; Hi-Z while CS is high CS (35), in Active low; a register write is decoded on the CS rising edge D0 to D7 (46 to 39), out Parallel data lanes, not used by the driver Control pins ¶ Pin (number) What it does Driver use CONVST (50), in The falling edge samples all channels ConvstWrite() : high for 1 µs, then low DRDY/ALARM (49), out Data ready, active high by default; can carry the window-comparator alert instead DrdyRead() , polled every 1 µs up to DRDY_TIMEOUT_US RESET (32), in Active-low asynchronous reset Not driven: tie it high (to IOVDD) or give it its own GPIO REFSEL (31), in High: internal 4.096 V reference. Low: external reference on REFIO Not driven: tie it high for the internal reference The driver resets the chip with the SW_RST bit in GEN_CFG1, so the RESET pin can stay high. If you leave REFSEL low without an external reference on REFIO, the chip powers down (SBASB22 section 7.3.6). Bus settings ¶ Setting Value Mode SPI mode 0 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 0), MSB first: SDI is latched on the rising edge, SCLK ends low before CS rises Clock Up to 60 MHz (f SCLK ); the ESP32-C6 examples use 8 MHz Register frame 24 bits: 8-bit address, 16-bit data; CS low for the whole frame Conversion read One CS-low burst: 16 bits per channel, 32 bytes for 16 channels (48 bytes with 24-bit words) Chip select High at least 16 ns between frames; 16 ns setup to the first edge and hold after the last I/O levels V IH ≥ 0.7 × IOVDD, V IL ≤ 0.3 × IOVDD The mode follows from the timing requirements (SDI captured on the rising edge, CS hold measured from the last falling edge); the datasheet does not name an SPI mode. Throughput in 1-lane mode ¶ Sixteen 16-bit words on one lane take 256 SCLK cycles. At the 60 MHz maximum that is 4.3 µs per snapshot, so 1-lane mode cannot exceed about 230 kSPS per channel, not the chip's 1 MSPS; at 8 MHz it is 32 µs, under 31 kSPS. These figures count clock cycles only; the conversion time, CS gaps and software overhead lower them further. Fewer channels ( SetChannelCountMode() ) or the parallel lanes raise the rate; the driver supports only 1-lane capture. One snapshot on the wire ¶ sequenceDiagram participant H as Host (driver) participant C as ADS9324 H->>C: CONVST high, 1 µs, then low (all 16 channels sampled) Note over C: conversion, t_CONV = 1.25 µs C-->>H: DRDY rises H->>C: CS low, 256 SCLK with SDI = 0 C-->>H: SDOUT: AIN1, AIN2 ... AIN16, 16 bits each, MSB first H->>C: CS high Timing ¶ Parameter Value Where the driver handles it Power-up time t PU (1 µF on REFCAP) 30 ms EnsureInitialized() waits POWER_ON_DELAY_MS = 30 Wait after software reset 1 ms (optional, Table 7-18) RESET_DELAY_MS = 1 CONVST high and low time at least 50 ns each The driver holds CONVST high for 1 µs Conversion time t CONV , no oversampling 1.25 µs DRDY poll, or CONV_FALLBACK_US = 10 µs without DRDY CONVST rate f CONVST 0.1 MHz to 1 MHz See the note below Sampling rate and the specifications The datasheet specifies the ADC for a CONVST rate of 100 kHz to 1 MHz. ReadSnapshot() issues one CONVST per call, so a slow polling loop runs the chip below that range. The conversions still complete; the datasheet's dynamic performance figures are not guaranteed there. Power ¶ Supply (pins) Range Current at full rate, typ / max AVDD_5V (26, 27, 56) 4.75 V to 5.25 V 30 mA / 35 mA AVDD_1V8 (30, 51) 1.7 V to 1.9 V 32 mA / 38 mA IOVDD (34, 47) 1.7 V to 3.6 V 6 mA / 10 mA Total dissipation is 230 mW typical, 295 mW maximum, at full throughput; standby ( SetPowerDown(true) ) is about 6.5 mW. There is no power-up sequence requirement. Decouple each supply pin with 1 µF and 0.1 µF to GND. Match IOVDD to your MCU's I/O voltage. The reference needs 4.7 µF from REFIO to REFM (pin 53) and 1 µF X7R between REFCAPA and REFM (pins 52 and 53) and between REFCAPB and REFM (pins 29 and 28). Connect REFM, GND and the thermal pad to the ground plane. Analog inputs ¶ Limit Value Input impedance 1 MΩ typical (0.8 MΩ to 1.2 MΩ) on each of AIN n P and AIN n M Full-scale ranges (AIN n P − AIN n M) ±2.5, ±5, ±6.25, ±10, ±12.5 V Common-mode range, differential ±12.5 V Operating input voltage, differential –17 V to +17 V on each pin Operating input voltage, single-ended AIN n P –13 V to +13 V, AIN n M –0.5 V to +0.5 V Absolute maximum, AIN n P and AIN n M ±18 V; 10 mA per pin Low-pass filter (–3 dB) 25.5 kHz (low bandwidth) or 280 kHz to 350 kHz (wide, by range) Match the source resistance on AIN n P with the same resistance on AIN n M to cancel the offset it adds. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 12+ or a current MSVC. No RTOS, heap or exceptions: every driver call is noexcept and returns bool or a result struct. Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-ads9324-driver.git external/hf-ads9324-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-ads9324-driver Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-ads9324-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf::ads9324 ) hf::ads9324 is an INTERFACE target: it carries the include directories ( inc/ , src/ for ads9324.ipp , and the generated version header) and requires C++20 ( cxx_std_20 ), so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect HF_ADS9324_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF Adds -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic to targets that link the driver HF_ADS9324_BUILD_HOST_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests and the documentation snippets in tests/ ( Testing and CI ) The project also installs a CMake package: after cmake --install , find_package(hf_ads9324) provides the same hf::ads9324 target. ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_ads9324/ . Copy that folder into your project's components/ (or point EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at it) and set the HF_ADS9324_ROOT cache variable to the driver checkout; the wrapper stops with a clear message when the path is wrong. Your component then declares REQUIRES hf_ads9324 . docs.text: PGA and calibration ¶ What each channel's analog front end can be set to, how the driver encodes it, and how to use the offset and gain correction registers. Table and equation numbers refer to the ADS9324 datasheet (SBASB22). Input type and range ¶ Each channel has its own PGA. ChannelConfig::type and ChannelConfig::range select it (Table 7-1): InputType CM_RANGE Input Differential (default) 000b AIN n P − AIN n M, common mode up to ±12.5 V SingleEnded 101b AIN n P against AIN n M at ground (±0.5 V) SingleEndedOpenWireSafe 110b Single-ended; with a pull-down on AIN n P, a disconnected source reads closest to code 0 (section 7.3.7) InputRange INPUT_RANGE Full scale (V) 1 LSB (µV) PlusMinus2V5 010b ±2.5 76.3 PlusMinus5V (default) 000b ±5 152.6 PlusMinus6V25 011b ±6.25 190.7 PlusMinus10V 100b ±10 305.2 PlusMinus12V5 101b ±12.5 381.5 1 LSB is 2 × FS / 65536. Every range is bipolar; the driver converts a count with V = count × FS / 32768 ( TwosToVoltage() ), using the range it last wrote to that channel. ChannelConfig::common_mode_correct sets CME_CORR_EN , the common-mode error correction the datasheet uses for its CMRR figures. How a channel is written ¶ Two channels share one PGA_CONFIG_AINx_y register, one byte each: Bits (per byte) Field 7 CME_CORR_EN 6:4 CM_RANGE[2:0] 3 reserved 2:0 INPUT_RANGE[2:0] The even local channel (AIN1, AIN3 ...) is the low byte, the odd one the high byte. ConfigureChannel() reads the register, replaces its byte and writes it back, then does the same with its two bits of PGA_BW_SEL . Configuring one channel therefore never changes its neighbour. Filter bandwidth ¶ ChannelConfig::bandwidth sets the low-pass filter after the PGA (Table 7-2): PgaBandwidth Range –3 dB corner Low (default) all 25.5 kHz Wide ±2.5 V 280 kHz Wide ±5 V 325 kHz Wide ±6.25 V 300 kHz Wide ±10 V, ±12.5 V 350 kHz Use Low unless the signal has content above about 10 kHz; it removes more noise and aliasing. Offset correction ¶ SetChannelOffset(channel, ofs) writes the 10-bit two's-complement OFS_AINn register. The chip adds it in quarter LSBs, before the gain (Equation 1): output = (code × 4 + OFS) / 4 OFS (register) Effect 0x1FF (+511) +127.75 LSB 0x100 (+256) +64 LSB 0x001 (+1) +0.25 LSB 0x3FF (−1) −0.25 LSB 0x200 (−512) −128 LSB To remove an offset of e LSB measured with the input shorted, write −4 × e . The range is −128 to +127.75 LSB. Gain correction ¶ SetChannelGain(channel, gan) writes the 14-bit two's-complement GAN_AINn register. The chip multiplies the offset-corrected code by 1 + GAN / 65536 (register description of GAN_AINn , Equation 2): GAN Multiplier 0x0000 1.000000 (reset value) 0x1FFF (+8191) 1.124985 0x2000 (−8192) 0.875000 The range is about ±12.5 %. For a channel that reads a factor k too high, write GAN = −(k − 1) / k × 65536 , close to −(k − 1) × 65536 for small errors. gan is a uint16_t : pass a negative value cast to uint16_t ; the driver keeps the low 14 bits. The API guide shows both calls. On-chip calibration ¶ The ADS9324 can also measure and correct its own offset and gain ( ADC_CAL , section 7.3.10), reducing the offset error from about ±30 LSB to ±8 LSB in the datasheet's example. The driver does not run it; the register address is reg::ADC_CAL if you write the sequence yourself.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing two small classes: one for SPI, one for CONVST, DRDY and delays. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls six methods on classes you derive from ads9324::SpiInterface<Self> and ads9324::HostInterface<Self> (in inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp ). The base classes use CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions, no vtable and nothing to allocate. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one ADS9324 object, whose public methods are listed from inc/ads9324.hpp. The core packs 24-bit register frames, selects register banks, merges the PGA nibbles and unpacks conversion bursts. It reaches the hardware only through two CRTP contracts in inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp: SpiInterface (one transfer method) and HostInterface (CONVST, DRDY and two delays). The platform port is the only code you write: two small classes, or one class implementing both. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/ads9324.hpp ADS9324 public methods ; inc/ads9324_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface, HostInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method Class Contract transfer(tx, rx, len) SpiInterface One full-duplex transfer of len bytes with CS low for all of them. tx == nullptr : send zeros. rx == nullptr : discard the received bytes ConvstWrite(high) HostInterface Drive CONVST high ( true ) or low ( false ) DrdyRead() HostInterface Return true when DRDY/ALARM is high (conversion ready) HasDrdy() const HostInterface true if DRDY is wired; false makes the driver wait CONV_FALLBACK_US instead DelayUs(us) HostInterface Block for at least us microseconds (1 µs steps during the DRDY poll) DelayMs(ms) HostInterface Block for at least ms milliseconds (30 ms power-up, 1 ms after reset) The port ¶ my_port.hpp // SPI: one CS-low window per call, SPI mode 0, MSB first. class MySpi : public ads9324 :: SpiInterface < MySpi > { public : // tx == nullptr: clock out zeros. rx == nullptr: discard what arrives on SDOUT. void transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) { platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } }; // Host: the CONVST output, the optional DRDY input and two delays. class MyHost : public ads9324 :: HostInterface < MyHost > { public : static constexpr int kConvst = 3 ; // GPIO wired to CONVST (pin 50) static constexpr int kDrdy = 11 ; // GPIO wired to DRDY/ALARM (pin 49) void ConvstWrite ( bool high ) { platform_gpio_write ( kConvst , high ); } bool DrdyRead () { return platform_gpio_read ( kDrdy ); } // high = conversion done bool HasDrdy () const { return true ; } // false: fixed wait instead void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) { platform_delay_us ( us ); } void DelayMs ( uint32_t ms ) { platform_delay_us ( ms * 1000U ); } }; One class may implement both contracts; pass the same object twice: ADS9324<Bus, Bus> adc(bus, bus) . Rules for the transfer ¶ SPI mode 0 , MSB first, up to 60 MHz. Start at 1 to 8 MHz on a new board. One CS window per call. CS goes low before the first byte and high after the last. Register frames are 3 bytes; a conversion burst is 32 bytes (16 channels, 16-bit words) or 48 bytes (24-bit words). Never split one call into several CS windows: the chip decodes a register write on the CS rising edge. Handle nullptr . The driver passes real buffers today, but the contract allows either pointer to be null. Own the bus. Do not share this CS with another device, and do not let another task use the bus in the middle of a register read (two frames). transfer() returns void , so the driver cannot learn about a bus error. Log or count errors in your port. CONVST and DRDY ¶ The driver holds CONVST high for 1 µs and then drives it low; the falling edge samples every channel. The chip needs only 50 ns high and 50 ns low, so any GPIO is fast enough. DRDY is active high by default; if your board inverts it, invert it in DrdyRead() , not with SetAlarmPin(..., true) . Without DRDY ( HasDrdy() returns false ) the driver waits CONV_FALLBACK_US (10 µs) after the falling edge. The conversion takes 1.25 µs without oversampling, so the default leaves margin. Reference implementation ¶ The ESP32 examples use esp32_ads9324_bus.hpp : one class that implements both contracts with the ESP-IDF spi_master driver (hardware CS, one transaction per call), GPIO for CONVST and DRDY, esp_rom_delay_us() and FreeRTOS delays. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the port on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over it. Call EnsureInitialized() . If it fails, print ReadDeviceId() : 0x0004 proves SDI, SCLK, CS and SDOUT end to end. Short one input and read a snapshot: the count should be within a few tens of LSB of zero. Watch GetDiagnostics().errors : it should stay at zero on a healthy link. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each ADS9324 one owner task, or guard every call on a driver object (and its port) with one mutex. Several chips on separate buses can run in parallel.

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Read all 16 inputs of an ADS9324 from your MCU: wire seven signals, write two small port classes, call three driver functions. 1. Wire it ¶ MCU ADS9324 (pin) Notes SPI SCLK SCLK (37) SPI mode 0; up to 60 MHz, start at 1 to 8 MHz SPI MOSI SDI (36) Register frames, zeros during a conversion read SPI MISO SDOUT (38) Register read-back and, in the driver's mode, conversion data SPI CS CS (35) Active low; one CS-low window per transfer GPIO out CONVST (50) The falling edge samples all channels GPIO in DRDY/ALARM (49) Optional; active high when a conversion is ready IOVDD RESET (32), REFSEL (31) RESET is active low: hold it high. REFSEL high selects the internal reference GND GND Common ground; also the thermal pad The ADS9324 needs three supplies (5 V, 1.8 V and the 1.7 V to 3.6 V I/O rail) and its reference capacitors before it answers. The Hardware page has the full pin list, the supplies and the timing. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the hf::ads9324 CMake target (or add inc/ and src/ to your include path and build with C++20). Installation covers CMake and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-ads9324-driver.git external/hf-ads9324-driver 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code: one SPI transfer, the CONVST and DRDY pins, and two delays. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp // SPI: one CS-low window per call, SPI mode 0, MSB first. class MySpi : public ads9324 :: SpiInterface < MySpi > { public : // tx == nullptr: clock out zeros. rx == nullptr: discard what arrives on SDOUT. void transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) { platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } }; // Host: the CONVST output, the optional DRDY input and two delays. class MyHost : public ads9324 :: HostInterface < MyHost > { public : static constexpr int kConvst = 3 ; // GPIO wired to CONVST (pin 50) static constexpr int kDrdy = 11 ; // GPIO wired to DRDY/ALARM (pin 49) void ConvstWrite ( bool high ) { platform_gpio_write ( kConvst , high ); } bool DrdyRead () { return platform_gpio_read ( kDrdy ); } // high = conversion done bool HasDrdy () const { return true ; } // false: fixed wait instead void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) { platform_delay_us ( us ); } void DelayMs ( uint32_t ms ) { platform_delay_us ( ms * 1000U ); } }; HasDrdy() returning false makes the driver wait a fixed time after CONVST instead of polling DRDY. Porting explains each method. 4. Read the channels ¶ main.cpp #include "ads9324.hpp" int read_all_16_channels ( MySpi & spi , MyHost & host ) { ads9324 :: ADS9324 < MySpi , MyHost > adc ( spi , host ); if ( ! adc . EnsureInitialized ()) { // 1. reset, 1-lane SDOUT, DEVICE_ID return -1 ; // wiring, supplies or SPI mode } ads9324 :: ChannelConfig cfg ; // 2. every input: differential, ±10 V cfg . type = ads9324 :: InputType :: Differential ; cfg . range = ads9324 :: InputRange :: PlusMinus10V ; if ( ! adc . ConfigureAllChannels ( cfg )) { return -2 ; } const ads9324 :: Snapshot snap = adc . ReadSnapshot (); // 3. CONVST, wait DRDY, read 32 bytes if ( ! snap . ok ()) { return -3 ; // snap.error says why } std :: printf ( "AIN1 = %.4f V \n " , static_cast < double > ( snap . voltage [ 0 ])); // 4. channel 0 is AIN1 return 0 ; } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() waits 30 ms for the supplies and reference, resets the chip, writes GEN_CFG3 = 0x0032 (1 lane, 16-bit words, data on SDOUT) and checks DEVICE_ID = 0x0004 . Nothing else works until it returns true . ConfigureAllChannels() writes each channel's PGA nibble and filter bit. The ranges are bipolar; the driver remembers them to convert counts to volts. ReadSnapshot() pulses CONVST, waits for DRDY, then clocks 32 bytes out of SDOUT in one CS-low window. Channel 0 in the API is AIN1 on the chip; channel 15 is AIN16. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check EnsureInitialized() returns false ReadDeviceId() : 0x0000 means no SDOUT data (wiring, SPI mode, supplies); anything else but 0x0004 means a framing problem Snapshot error Timeout CONVST wiring, DRDY polarity, or set HasDrdy() to false All counts near zero Input type and range, a floating input in open-wire-safe mode, or the AIN x M pin not connected Voltages off by a fixed factor The range you configured is not the range you assumed ( PGA and calibration ) Next ¶ API guide : per-channel set-up, calibration, window comparator, errors. Porting explains each method.

docs.text: main.cpp #include "ads9324.hpp" int read_all_16_channels ( MySpi & spi , MyHost & host ) { ads9324 :: ADS9324 < MySpi , MyHost > adc ( spi , host ); if ( ! adc . EnsureInitialized ()) { // 1. reset, 1-lane SDOUT, DEVICE_ID return -1 ; // wiring, supplies or SPI mode } ads9324 :: ChannelConfig cfg ; // 2. every input: differential, ±10 V cfg . type = ads9324 :: InputType :: Differential ; cfg . range = ads9324 :: InputRange :: PlusMinus10V ; if ( ! adc . ConfigureAllChannels ( cfg )) { return -2 ; } const ads9324 :: Snapshot snap = adc . ReadSnapshot (); // 3. CONVST, wait DRDY, read 32 bytes if ( ! snap . ok ()) { return -3 ; // snap.error says why } std :: printf ( "AIN1 = %.4f V \n " , static_cast < double > ( snap . voltage [ 0 ])); // 4. channel 0 is AIN1 return 0 ; } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() waits 30 ms for the supplies and reference, resets the chip, writes GEN_CFG3 = 0x0032 (1 lane, 16-bit words, data on SDOUT) and checks DEVICE_ID = 0x0004 . Nothing else works until it returns true . ConfigureAllChannels() writes each channel's PGA nibble and filter bit. The ranges are bipolar; the driver remembers them to convert counts to volts. ReadSnapshot() pulses CONVST, waits for DRDY, then clocks 32 bytes out of SDOUT in one CS-low window. Channel 0 in the API is AIN1 on the chip; channel 15 is AIN16. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers.

docs.text: Registers and SPI frames ¶ What the driver sends over SPI: the 24-bit register frame, the three register banks, the two-frame read and the conversion burst. Section and table numbers refer to the ADS9324 datasheet (SBASB22). The addresses are constants in inc/ads9324_registers.hpp (namespace ads9324::reg ). The register frame ¶ Every register access is one 24-bit frame, MSB first, CS low for all 24 clocks: Bits 23:16 15:0 SDI Register address 16-bit data SDI is latched on the SCLK rising edge; the write is decoded when CS rises (section 7.5.1). reg::PackWrite(addr, data) builds the frame. Register banks ¶ The 16-bit registers sit in three banks addressed with 8 bits. BANK_SEL (address 0x02 ) is reachable from every bank and selects which one later addresses decode in: BANK_SEL value Bank Holds 0x0001 Common GEN_CFG1 to GEN_CFG5, PDN_CTL, DRDY_ALARM_SEL, ANA_CFG½, ADC_CAL, DEVICE_ID 0x0002 AIN1 to AIN8 PGA_CONFIG, PGA_BW_SEL, OFS, GAN, DWC registers of channels 1 to 8 0x0004 AIN9 to AIN16 The same for channels 9 to 16 The two channel banks have the same layout. API channel n (0 to 15) is in bank AIN1-8 when n < 8, with local index n mod 8 ( reg::BankForChannel() , reg::LocalChannel() ). The driver writes BANK_SEL only when the bank changes. Reading a register ¶ A read takes two frames (Table 7-17): Frame SDI[23:16] SDI[15:0] SDOUT 1 0x01 (GEN_CFG1) REG_ADDR in bits 15:8, REG_RD_EN = 1 in bit 0 don't care 2 0x00 0x0000 Bits 23:8 = the register's data, bits 7:0 = 0 The driver selects the bank first, so a read costs two or three frames. reg::ReadCommand() and reg::UnpackRegData() build and unpack them. Registers the driver uses ¶ Common bank: Address Name Driver use 0x01 GEN_CFG1 SW_RST (bit 1) in SoftwareReset() ; register-read command 0x02 BANK_SEL Bank selection 0x08 PDN_CTL DEVICE_PDN (bit 0) in SetPowerDown() 0x0A GEN_CFG3 EN_OFS_BINARY (12), DOUT_LANE_SEL (5:4), DOUT_LENGTH (3:2), ADC_DATA_SDOUT_EN (1) 0x0C DRDY_ALARM_SEL ALRM_POL (4), DRDY_ALRM_SEL (3:0) in SetAlarmPin() 0x11 ANA_CFG2 ADC_CH_SEL (6:4), ADC_NUM_SEL (3:2) in SetChannelCountMode() 0x21 DEVICE_ID Read by ReadDeviceId() ; 0x0004 on an ADS9324 Channel banks (the same address in AIN1-8 and AIN9-16): Address Name Driver use 0x08 to 0x0B PGA_CONFIG_AINx_y Two channels per register, one byte each 0x0C PGA_BW_SEL Two bits per channel 0x11 to 0x18 OFS_AINn 10-bit offset 0x19 to 0x20 GAN_AINn 14-bit gain 0x21 DWC_CFG Window-comparator enable bit per channel 0x22 to 0x29 DWC_TH_AINn High threshold (15:8), low threshold (7:0) The other registers (reference select, oversampling filters, phase delay, ADC self-calibration, test patterns) have addresses in ads9324_registers.hpp but no driver call. PGA and calibration explains the channel registers. Initialisation sequence ¶ EnsureInitialized() follows Table 7-18, then checks the ID: Step Frame or action Why 1 Wait 30 ms Supplies and reference settle (t PU ) 2 GEN_CFG1 = 0x0002 Software reset 3 Wait 1 ms Reset settle 4 BANK_SEL = 0x0001 Common bank 5 GEN_CFG3 = 0x0032 1 lane, 16-bit words, conversion data on SDOUT 6 Read DEVICE_ID , expect 0x0004 Proves SDI, SDOUT, SCLK and CS work After reset the chip outputs conversion data on eight lanes (D0 to D7), which a plain SPI controller cannot read; step 5 is what makes SDOUT carry it. The conversion burst ¶ After CONVST and DRDY, the driver clocks one CS-low burst with SDI held at zero. Each channel is one word, MSB first, lowest channel first (Figure 5-5): Setting Word Burst for 16 channels DoutLength::Bits16 (default) 16 bits 32 bytes DoutLength::Bits24 24 bits; the driver keeps the top 16 48 bytes With the default two's-complement coding, 0 V is 0x0000 , the most positive code is 0x7FFF and −FS is 0x8000 . In offset-binary coding midscale is 0x8000 ; the driver converts it to two's complement, so Snapshot::count is always signed.

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against a model of the chip, compiled documentation, ESP32 builds and static analysis, on every pull request. Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a mock that implements both contracts: a register file for the three banks that answers the two-frame read, a CONVST edge counter and a canned conversion burst. No hardware or ESP-IDF is needed. cmake -S . -B build-host -DHF_ADS9324_BUILD_HOST_TESTS = ON cmake --build build-host ctest --test-dir build-host --output-on-failure File Covers tests/host/test_ads9324_protocol.cpp Frame packing, GEN_CFG3 value, PGA nibble encoding, bank mapping, the initialisation sequence and DEVICE_ID, channel configuration, offset and gain registers, power-down, snapshot unpacking, ReadChannel() errors Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target hf_ads9324_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. CI workflows ¶ Workflow What it checks Host unit tests GCC and Clang build and run the tests and the doc snippets ESP32 examples build Every CI-enabled app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type; clang-format and clang-tidy on the examples C++ lint, C++ analysis clang-format, clang-tidy and cppcheck Docs Strict site build, figure and generated-table drift, Doxygen, link check, Lighthouse budget Markdown lint, YAML lint, link check Repository text files The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of hf-general-ci-tools and hf-espidf-ci-tools . On hardware ¶ The driver_integration_test example is the hardware test suite: it runs initialisation, PGA, snapshot, calibration and power-down tests and prints a pass / fail summary over the serial monitor.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up an ADS9324, their causes and the fix for each, cheapest check first. Start with ReadDeviceId() and GetDiagnostics() : a correct DEVICE_ID ( 0x0004 ) proves the SPI link, so a remaining problem is in CONVST, DRDY or the channel settings. Initialisation ¶ Symptom Cause Fix ReadDeviceId() returns 0x0000 SDOUT not connected, chip not powered, RESET held low, or REFSEL low with no external reference (the chip powers down) Check the three supplies, tie RESET and REFSEL high ( Hardware ) DEVICE_ID is 0xFFFF or random Wrong SPI mode, MISO floating, CS released between bytes SPI mode 0, one CS window per transfer() , lower the clock DEVICE_ID right on the second call only The first frame went out before the supplies settled Keep POWER_ON_DELAY_MS at 30 or more; power the ADC before the MCU starts talking Snapshots ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Error::Timeout CONVST not reaching the chip, DRDY not wired, DRDY inverted, or DRDY/ALARM muxed to the comparator Scope CONVST and DRDY; SetAlarmPin(AlarmPinMode::Drdy) ; or HasDrdy() = false All counts 0 or -1 Conversion data still on D0 to D7 (8-lane reset mode), so SDOUT is idle Call EnsureInitialized() after every power cycle or hardware reset; do not change SetDigitalInterface() away from 1 lane on SDOUT Channels look shifted A reduced SetChannelCountMode() is active; the chip sends a fixed channel set Use ChannelCountMode::All16 ( API guide ) Values ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Voltage off by a fixed factor (2, 2.5, 4 ...) The driver's range for that channel is not the one the chip uses Configure the channel with ConfigureChannel() ; with a changed CONFIG_ADS9324_RANGE_* default, call ConfigureAllChannels() Large offset on a single-ended input AIN n M not at ground, or input type Differential with AIN n M floating Connect AIN n M to ground and use SingleEnded Offset changes with the source Source resistance on AIN n P not matched on AIN n M (1 MΩ input) Add an equal resistor on AIN n M, then trim with SetChannelOffset() A disconnected sensor reads a random value Input type SingleEnded without a pull-down Use SingleEndedOpenWireSafe and a pull-down ( PGA and calibration ) Noise higher than expected Wide bandwidth selected, or missing reference capacitors PgaBandwidth::Low ; 4.7 µF on REFIO, 1 µF on REFCAPA and REFCAPB Gain correction makes it worse A negative correction passed as a large positive number outside 14 bits, or the sign inverted GAN = −(k − 1) / k × 65536 for a channel reading k times too high Still stuck ¶ Run the host tests to rule out the driver, then the driver_integration_test example on your board: it isolates each feature in its own test.
